description: Does the supervisor advance delegated work without asking and escalate only a real blocker (comms spec #acceptance-autonomous-local, #acceptance-real-blocker, #parent-notifications BLOCKED row; #875)? A lane supervisor at a goal check-in on fixture lane-shout-wip, whose tests/test_cli.py really fails `ruff format --check` (the recoverable local validation failure), with ticket #15 ready and unassigned (the independent ready work). Herdr and its kit wrappers are stand-ins answering delivered (schema.md, Case, stand_ins); octo-feather-handoff is the real encoder. Graded on the supervisor's runs (schema.md, Run record): herdr-say --parent none for the local failure, alone or reported BLOCKED by a worker, and exactly one for an owner-held access blocker; herdr-spawn of #15's implementer, named <role>-<ticket> (comms spec #transport-spawn-name). Who carries the repair is the supervisor's call (a fresh implementer, or #15's, one writer of tests/test_cli.py), so no fact names its worker: the brief that assigns it is copied into the evidence. owner-access-blocker-message is the review twin of owner-access-blocker-and-ready-work: whether that one message is an actionable access decision naming the blocked branch, attempts and options has no fact. The lane's evidence is graded where it is kept: the qa sandbox masks lane state outside the case repo, so each task names the run's hand-off log in the repo, notes/gh12.handoffs.jsonl, and branch_paths reads that it changed (its lines are copied into the evidence). Stated limits: a message to the director by pane id instead of --parent is not counted; the tasks never name the director's pane.
